findings.description: F001 declares the listed guarded commands to be the complete plan-mutating surface, but F002 and F003 introduce or modify plan worktree remove and plan worktree create, both of which mutate registry or worktree state. The plan needs an explicit decision that these commands are exempt from the wrong-worktree guard, or they need equivalent guard coverage.
findings.recommendation: Pin create/remove as intentionally outside the wrong-worktree guard with rationale and regression tests, or add them to the guarded entry-point matrix.

findings.description: F002 requires audit-first deletion, but the described audit record appears to encode a successful removal before the destructive git worktree remove step has actually succeeded. The registry-only completion path then relies on an audit log entry for successful removal, which can be ambiguous after partial failures.
findings.recommendation: Separate removal intent from removal completion, or pin the completion predicate so a pre-delete audit entry cannot be mistaken for proof that deletion succeeded.

findings.description: F003 asserts that no symlinks are created in the new worktree, but it does not pin behavior when an allowlisted source file or preexisting target path is itself a symlink. That leaves a deterministic-rule gap for the no-symlinks-in-v1 policy and for copy-time overwrite refusal.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit refusal and reporting rules for symlinked allowlist source or target entries, with tests covering both cases.
